title: Springboard cross-functional sprint charter and all-hands playbook (Q2 2029) - WIP
content:
Purpose
-----
This is a working charter for a condensed cross-functional sprint ("Springboard") that runs in the three weeks leading into Q2 FY29 and culminates in a compact all-hands + exec sync. The aim: align around 3 measurable company-level objectives, surface risks, land immediate execution owners, and create a short list of experiments (not features) that materially improve inference economics or observability by the end of Q2.

Scope and constraints
---------------------
- Scope: company-level framing, 3 top objectives, comms runbook for a 90-minute all-hands, and a 1-page exec update template.
- Not in scope: detailed engineering sprint plans, individual product roadmaps, hiring decisions.
- Constraint: Keep commitments to outcomes achievable with current headcount + up to 20% contractor burst for May-June.

Timing (high level)
-------------------
- Week 0 (Mar 25–31): intake + hypothesis collection (product, infra, sales, CS).
- Week 1 (Apr 1–7): prioritize experiments and form 6 cross-functional pods (2-week charters).
- Week 2 (Apr 8–14): execution spike, baseline metrics, first drafts of exec update.
- All-hands rehearsal (Apr 15) -> All-hands (Apr 18) -> Exec report (Apr 19).

Company-level draft OKRs (hypothesis-driven)
--------------------------------------------
Objective A — Reduce per-token inference cost for typical web-traffic routes by measurable margin
- KR A1: 12% reduction in median per-token cost for hosted-api routes where 90th percentile latency <= 300ms.
- KR A2: 25% increase in cache hit ratio (prefix + KV) on top 20 customer workloads.
- KR A3: A/B test shows no >3% regression in top-5 prompt quality metrics for recommended quantization profiles.

Objective B — Improve production reliability and graceful degradation during peak bursts
- KR B1: <1% user-facing error rate during simulated 3x traffic bursts for Dedicated customers.
- KR B2: Rollout canary fallback success rate of 98% across region failover tests.
- KR B3: Reduce mean-time-to-detect (MTTD) for inference SLO violations to <90s with new alerting hooks.

Objective C — Developer velocity: shorten time-to-ship small inference optimizations
- KR C1: Two-step developer flow for model rollout -> canary -> promote reduced to 3 clicks in Console.
- KR C2: Ship 4 workload-aware optimizer recommendations (batching or quantization) with one-click apply.
- KR C3: Adoption: 30% of active teams have applied at least one recommendation by end of Q2.

Hypothesis and experiments (examples)
------------------------------------
- Hypothesis 1: Small changes to default batching window reduce tail latency at high concurrency without hurting median — experiment: tune batching window on 3 high-volume routes and measure cost/latency.
- Hypothesis 2: Introduce a light-weight prefix cache that keeps hot prefixes in host memory to cut token generation for specific product flows — experiment: 2-week spike with auto-rollback.
- Hypothesis 3: Console microflow for one-click quantization profile application will increase adoption — experiment: prototype + 5 customer trials.

All-hands run-of-show (90 minutes)
----------------------------------
- 0:00–0:05 Welcome (CEO) — framing: what we must achieve this quarter and why it matters to customers.
- 0:05–0:20 Exec snapshot (CTO + Head of Product) — top 3 OKRs + 60-second status on each.
- 0:20–0:35 Field report (Customer Success) — signals: customers asking for cost/latency improvements; highlight 2 case studies.
- 0:35–0:55 Demo & quick wins (ENG + DX) — show the new Console microflow + a caching spike result.
- 0:55–1:10 Breakout review (pre-collected pods) — 3x 5-minute pod highlights (pod leads pre-record).
- 1:10–1:25 AMA + decisions (panel: CEO, CTO, Head of Eng) — live questions triaged; close with decisions we need from execs.
- 1:25–1:30 Close & next steps (VP Operations) — distribution plan for exec update, required follow-ups.

Roles & owners (first-pass)
---------------------------
- Program lead: Aisha Patel (company-ops) — overall coordinator, runbooks, gate for exec slide set.
- CTO sponsor: Marco Delgado — technical verifications, SLO approvals.
- Product sponsor: Ruth Kim — OKR alignment and prioritization.
- CS lead: Sofia Alvarez — customer case studies and feedback loop.
- 6 Pod leads (to be named) — accountable for a 2-week experiment charter and a 1-slide pod summary.

Communication & pre-reads
------------------------
- Pre-read (distributed Apr 12): 1-pager with OKRs, 3 experiment briefs, and a 2-line ask for each exec (resource/time).
- Slack channel: #springboard-q2-2029 (create Apr 1). Use for daily standups and quick escalations.
- Confluence: draft page linked in linked_artifacts for experiment artifacts and pod notes.

Risk register (top 5)
---------------------
1) Overcommit: too many pods -> diluted impact. Mitigation: cap to 6 pods, each with a single measurable metric.
2) Regressions in output quality due to quantization: mitigation: require A/B and rollback guard rails in runtime.
3) Customer disruption during canary/fallback tests: mitigation: notify dedicated customers, schedule low-traffic windows.
4) Observability gaps preventing MTTD improvements: mitigation: 2-week instrumentation spike prioritized.
5) Exec bandwidth: mitigation: short decision templates, pre-committed time blocks for exec reviews.

Decision points for execs (what we need now)
----------------------------------------------
- Approve up to 20% contractor budget for May–June to accelerate spikes (ask: OK/no OK).
- Greenlight low-risk canary tests on Dedicated customers with explicit opt-out (ask: agree to opt-out policy).
- Confirm CTO will sign off on SLO targets for the Springboard KRs by Apr 10.

Meeting artifacts to produce
--------------------------
- 1-page exec update (template) — due Apr 14 (owner: Aisha).
- 6x 1-slide pod summaries — due Apr 13 (pod leads).
- All-hands slide deck + speaker notes + rehearsal checklist — due Apr 15 (owner: Commops).

Checklist (pre-launch)
----------------------
- [ ] Pods named and leads assigned (due Apr 1)
- [ ] Slack channel created (Apr 1)
- [ ] Pre-read drafted and shared (Apr 12)
- [ ] All-hands logistics booked + AV check (Apr 14)
- [ ] Exec sign-offs on contractor and canary policies (Apr 10)

Open questions / parking lot
--------------------------
- Do we want a small budget line for customer incentives (discounts/credits) for participating in canaries? (Ops + Rev ops)
- How do we measure "developer velocity" consistently across Product and DX? propose: time-to-apply-recommendation metric.
- Should we publish a short public blog post (marketing) summarizing outcomes at end of Q2, or keep learnings internal?

Next immediate actions (this week)
---------------------------------
- Aisha: finalize pod intake form and circulate (Mar 25).
- Marco: sign off initial SLO targets draft (Mar 27).
- Ruth: convene Product prioritization sync (Mar 26).
- Sofia: identify two customer case studies willing to participate (Mar 29).

Notes to reviewers
------------------
This is intentionally compact and experiment-focused. We are not trying to expand the roadmap; we want a tight set of measurable bets that shift cost/latency economics and prove the operational playbook. Please add comments inline in this doc, flag any blockers you foresee, and sign up to lead a pod if you care about one of the hypothesis areas.

Parking-lot artifacts that may be attached later
------------------------------------------------
- Draft console microflow mockups (Figma link placeholder).
- Instrumentation plan for MTTD (SRE spike ticket).
- Customer communication templates for opt-in/opt-out canary flows.
